outlook.statement: The Company is aggressively expanding its global market footprint, optimizing plant-level energy utilization, and shifting focus toward in-house designed, high-margin value-added products. Through the implementation of the aforementioned measures, the Company expects to achieve an approximate 10% to 15% improvement in operational efficiencies, which is projected to proportionately elevate net profit margins over the ensuing financial cycles.
The Company continues its journey of delivering value to its customers. It adopted several significant external benchmarks and certifications.

The Thermoformed Plastic Products market is anticipated to exhibit fluctuating growth patterns in the near term, largely influenced by persistent factors that contributed to sluggish growth in 2023. However, improvements in the wider economy and the alleviation of supply chain concerns are projected to facilitate a rebound in market demand, particularly in the latter half of 2026.

Dedicated efforts are underway to return the business to a strong growth path in the coming financial year 2026–27. The Company expects tremendous progress, driven by our newly in-house designed, value-added products.

risks: Inflationary pressures on standard operating costs, freight, and severe raw material price fluctuations impact net margins.

The Company has adequate internal controls in place at various functional level and does not foresee any major risk such as financial, credit, legal, regulatory and other risk keeping in view the nature and size of its business.

Presence of unorganized players and reprocessed products challenging the market through unethical practices such as providing substandard products made from lower-grade materials and exploiting consumer lack of awareness

The Company does not carry commodity price risks and Commodity hedging activities.

key_audit_matters: Revenue Recognition - Sale of Goods is recognized when control of the goods has been transferred to the customers, depending on individual terms at an amount which the Company is expected to receive for those goods or services. Thus, Revenue Recognition from sale of Goods involves key judgments relating to identification of distinct performance obligations, determination of the transaction price, allocation of the transaction price to identified performance obligations, and the appropriateness of the revenue recognition methodology. Also the Company's profit is dependent on proper accounting of Revenue and is therefore susceptible to misstatement. Cut off is the key assertion in so far as revenue recognition is concerned, since an inappropriate cut-off can result in material misstatement of results for the year.

Revenue Recognition - Sale of Goods is recognized when control of the goods has been transferred to the customers, depending on individual terms at an amount which the Holding Company is expected to receive for those goods or services. Revenue Recognition from sale of Goods involves key judgments relating to identification of distinct performance obligations, determination of the transaction price, allocation of the transaction price to identified performance obligations, and the appropriateness of the revenue recognition methodology. Cut off is the key assertion.
